header: This decides whether a circular is a ROSTER (a health check-up schedule: a ruled table of T.No / Name / Deptt.Code / Department, with the date printed once per group of rows). I decide it from the PAGES, not from the headline the uploader typed. I do it in two steps, cheapest first:

1. STRUCTURE (image only, about a second a page): a ruled table whose last column is cut into MERGED cells, far fewer than the rows beside them (a roster prints each date once for a whole group of rows; an ordinary table has a rule on every row in every column). Pages of letters and ordinary tables fail here, so an ordinary circular costs nothing but this look at its first few pages.

2. HEADINGS (Gemini's reading of ONE page, once per document): the top of the table must read like a roster's heading row: the TICKET column (T.No) and at least two of Name, Deptt, Department, Date, Code. A ruled table with date cells that is NOT a roster stops here and is read the normal way. (If the first roster-like page has no headings, being a continuation page, I try the next one before giving up.)

The probe looks at the first few pages only (ROSTER_DISCOVERY_PAGES): a circular that has shown no roster table by then is treated as an ordinary one, so no long document pays for a search it cannot need. Once a roster table is confirmed, I look at every later page too (the schedule may run to the last page, and the page after it may be a letter). Nothing here writes anything or changes how an ordinary page is read.

symbols.name: ROSTER_DISCOVERY_PAGES
doc: I look at only this many of a document's first pages to find a roster table.

symbols.name: analyzeRosterStructure
symbols.sig: export async function analyzeRosterStructure(png: Buffer): Promise<RosterStructure>
doc: Does the page have the STRUCTURE of a roster: a ruled table with a column of merged date cells? I look at the picture only.

symbols.name: HEADER_TEXT_CHARS
doc: This is how much of the page's text (Gemini's reading) I search for the heading row, because the heading row sits right below the title.

symbols.name: headerLooksLikeRosterText
doc: Do the first lines of the page's text read like a roster's heading row: the TICKET column (T.No) and at least two of Name, Deptt, Department, Date, Code? I require the ticket column so that a stray "name" or "date" in a table of something else cannot pass. The text is Gemini's reading of the page.

members.name: classify
members.sig: classify(png: Buffer, pageNo: number, readText: () => Promise<string>): Promise<RosterVerdict>;
doc: I classify page by page, in order. `readText` returns Gemini's reading of the page; I call it only for a page that LOOKS like a roster, to read its heading row.

members.name: isRoster
doc: null means undecided, true a roster circular, false an ordinary one

symbols.name: createRosterProbe
symbols.sig: export function createRosterProbe(opts: { discoveryPages?: number } = {}): RosterProbe

behaviours: a ruled table with merged date cells has the structure of a roster
a page of a letter does not (no ruled table)
an ordinary ruled table (a rule on every row in EVERY column, the last included) does not: its last column is not merged
a roster's heading row (T.NO, NAME, DEPTT. CODE, DEPARTMENT, DATE) reads like a roster's
the spellings count: 'T.No', 'Ticket No', 'Deptt.Code'
no ticket column: 'Name', 'Department', 'Date' alone is NOT a roster (a stray 'name' or 'date' in another table cannot pass)
a ticket column and only one other heading is not enough
an ordinary table's headings are not a roster's
an empty reading is not a roster
headings far down the page text (past the first lines) are ignored
a schedule circular: two letter pages, then the roster pages -> other, other, ROSTER, ROSTER, ROSTER
...it is a roster circular, and the heading OCR was used exactly ONCE for the whole document
after the roster, a letter page is an ordinary page again (the last page of a schedule may be a letter)
an ordinary circular (letters): every page is ordinary, and the OCR is never used
a table with merged date cells whose headings are NOT a roster's: ordinary pages, not a roster circular
...the headings were read only twice (two pages tried), never again
an ordinary ruled table (not merged) never reaches the OCR at all, even if its headings would read like a roster's
a first roster-like page without headings (a continuation page) does not end the search: the next page with headings confirms it
a roster table that first appears after page ${ROSTER_DISCOVERY_PAGES} is not looked for (a long circular does not pay for a search): ordinary, no OCR, not a roster
the discovery window can be set (2 pages)
if the heading OCR fails the probe throws (the upload route catches it and treats the page as ordinary)
